Land use change emissions were included for those pathways that use soybean, corn starch, and corn stover as the feedstocks. Methanol from woody biomass via gasification, RD from woody biomass via CFP (Pt/TiO ), and DME from woody biomass gasification have higher SO emissions: 49, 2 X 40, and 37 mg SO /MJ, respectively. For these pathways, SO mainly derives from process X X emissions during the conversion phase because the final fuel has no sulfur and the sulfur content in the feedstock is removed during the conversion process. As such, the SOx emissions are not expected at the tailpipe of the locomotive but should be evaluated during the fuel production process. Any SOx emission strategy from these fuels needs to be implemented in the refineries where the fuel is produced. Emission control strategies could include feedstock hydro- desulphurization and selective catalytic reduction of the stack gas in the refinery.
